prompt: PagerDuty is firing HostMemLow for web-prod-3, a 64G nginx+app box: MemFree fell from 34G to 1.2G between 01:00 and 02:30 and holds at 1.8%. On-call wants an emergency reboot before it OOMs, but app latency is normal and the nightly backup ran in that exact window. Determine whether an OOM is actually imminent and stop the pager storm.

payments-api on node k8s-node-14 has restarted three times since 09:00, exit code 137 each time. The node has 128G RAM with about 60G free the entire period, so the service team suspects kubelet is killing pods erroneously and filed a platform bug. Checkout p99 spikes for 40s at every restart. Find what is actually killing the container and stop the restarts.

quote-engine (Java 17, -Xmx4g) on quote-prod-2 is OOM-killed by systemd roughly every three days: the unit has MemoryMax=6G and RSS at kill is ~5.9G. The dev team insists the heap is capped at 4G so it cannot be their code, and asks for MemoryMax=12G. RSS is 5.6G right now and climbing. Find where the extra memory lives before approving anything.

ingestd, a C++ service with 64 worker threads on ingest-prod-5, grows from 2.1G RSS at deploy to 7.2G over a week and will hit its 8G container limit by Sunday. ASan and a week of valgrind in staging found zero leaks, and traffic is flat. RSS is 6.9G now. Explain the growth and get it back under 3G without a nightly restart cron.

cache-prod-1 (24G RAM) runs Redis 7: INFO reports used_memory 9.5G but process RSS is 19.2G, and the kernel OOM-killed redis-server once last week during the nightly BGSAVE. p99 rises from 1.2ms to 40ms while the save runs. Ops proposes doubling instance RAM. Explain the 2x RSS and fix it without new hardware.

The report-builder pod on the prod-batch cluster is OOMKilled (exit 137) every night at 02:10 while the report job runs. The container limit is 4Gi, but kubectl top and ps inside the container never show more than ~950Mi of process RSS, so the team calls it a kubelet accounting bug. Locate the invisible ~3G and stop the nightly kill.

etl-runner on etl-prod-2, a 32G host, loads a 6.1G feature dict in the parent then forks 8 multiprocessing workers. Since yesterday's data refresh the host hits 96% memory an hour into the run, and dmesg shows the kernel killed two workers overnight at anon-rss ~2.9G each. The devs added tracemalloc and it reports only 41MB per worker. Make the pool fit in memory.

gw-prod-7 (32G, 16 cores) serves api-gateway with p99 up from 40ms to 780ms since 06:00. CPU averages 31%, dmesg shows no OOM kills, free reports 2.8G available, error rates are flat — every dashboard is green except latency. A log-indexer service was deployed to this host yesterday evening. Find the bottleneck and restore gateway latency.

ci-runner-9 (64G) shows build times 3x baseline since Tuesday; jobs stall in allocation-heavy phases. Grafana reports 59G used, yet summing every process RSS gives only 6.1G, and there are no OOM kills. A reboot fixes it for about two days, so the fleet team wants a nightly reboot cron. Find where the other ~50G went and kill the regression properly.

tile-renderer v3.18 on maps-prod-6 aborts every ~8h: logs show mmap failed: Cannot allocate memory, then exit 134. Its cgroup shows memory.current 2.1G against an 8G limit and the host has 41G free, so infra bounced the ticket to the app team, who bounced it back. The current process is 6h old. Root-cause the ENOMEM and stop the crashes.

scoring-batch on ml-prod-4 dies at 03:00 with exit 137; dmesg confirms a memcg OOM at its 8G limit with anon-rss 7.9G. The host was given 16G of swap specifically so this job could spill, and free shows SwapFree 15.9G — yet the job never swapped a byte. Runs complete fine at smaller input scale. Make tonight's 8.4G run survive.

The istio-proxy sidecar in checkout pods on worker-32 (32G node) was OOM-killed six times today, exit 137, RSS ~180Mi each time — far under its 512Mi container limit. The checkout container itself never restarts. The mesh team is preparing an Envoy rollback. Latency degrades for minutes before each kill. Work out why envoy keeps dying and fix the right component.

pg-primary-2 (48G) lost postgres to the OOM killer at 03:10 two nights running — dmesg says Killed process (postgres), anon-rss ~9.4G — forcing failovers. Postgres has run for years at that footprint. The only recent change: the backup team installed snapvault-agent last week with 'OOM protection' enabled. Explain why the kernel chooses postgres and stop the 03:10 kills.

analytics-7 (64G) OOM-killed two batch workers this morning — dmesg shows constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE, anon-rss ~3.1G each — although the capacity dashboard sums all processes at 41G. MemAvailable is 1.9G. Nothing new deployed in a month, but the box was rebooted last night for kernel patching. Account for the missing ~20G and restore capacity.
